newsitem.title: USA: US corp debt ends mostly unchanged, no new issues.
newsitem.headline: US corp debt ends mostly unchanged, no new issues.

text.p: U.S. high-yield and high-grade corporate bonds ended Wednesday's session unchanged to a shade weaker in lazy trade while no new issues were priced in the secondary market, dealers and syndicate officials said.
Spreads on Philip Morris Co Inc notes due 2006 widened only a couple of basis points on news the cigarette maker hiked its quarterly dividend to $1.20 a share from $1.00.
Philip Morris notes due 2006 were quoted 93 bid, 87 offer, two basis points wider from Tuesday's close, dealers said.
Airline debt was pushed mildly higher after news of rate hikes by several airlines in an effort to cover the resumption of a 10 percent Federal excise tax.
United Air Lines 10.67 percent debentures due 2004 closed tighter by four basis points at 117 bid, 112 offer.
New banking sector debt issued on Tuesday held firm.
KeyCorp unit Key Bank's $165 million subordinated bank notes traded unchanged at 75 basis points, a trader said.
Swiss Bank Corp's 10-year and 30-year subordinated notes were quoted at the issue price of 53 and 77 basis point spreads, respectively.
In the junk bond arena, Century Communications 9-3/4 percent notes due 2002 fell 1/2 to 101-1/4 bid, 101-3/4 offer after the release of fourth quarter earnings.
Century lost $0.49 per share in the fourth quarter ended May 31, 1996, compared to a $0.42 loss in the same quarter a year prior.
Sprint Corp zero coupon debt gained 1/8 to a 56-3/8 bid. Nextel paper fell 1/4 to 58-3/4 bid, 59-1/4 offer. Ralph Grocery 11.0 percent notes also lost 1/4 to 97-1/2 bid, 98 offer.
The steel sector was quiet, one dealer said.

Teleport Communications Group's 9.875 percent notes were actively bid but closed unchanged at 100-1/2 bid, 100-3/4 offer. The notes gained one point on Tuesday as the company was seen as ripe for a takeover in the rapidly consolidating industry, analysts said.

Trump Hotels & Casino debt gained about one point following a Standard & Poor's rating upgrade late Tuesday, traders said. Trump Atlantic City 11.25 percent first mortgage notes due 2006 were up about one point at 96 bid, 96-1/4 offer.

Standard & Poor's upgraded the Trump Hotels & Casino $155 million 15.5 percent senior secured notes due 2005 to B-plus from B-minus. S&P said the upgrade reflected good initial operating results at the firm's Indiana riverboat casino. For the firm generated $8.6 million of revenues and $2.5 million of earnings EBITA.
Trump Castle debt traded up one point at 95, a trader said.

Grand Casinos Inc 10.125 percent first mortgage notes were marginally weaker at 97 bid, 97-1/2 offer in quiet trade. The debt gyrated in a one point range on Tuesday after news the firm would take a charge against future earnings as a result of operating losses at 42 percent-owned Stratosphere.
The corporate primary market was slow ahead of the Labor Day holiday and next week's release of August employment data, according to syndicate sources.
Dealers said they expected supply to build in September, especially if the Treasury market can rally on jobs data.
--Roanne Daniels, 212-859-1677
